question: Can a single LLM improve its own outputs at test time by generating feedback on them and refining iteratively, with no training?
hypothesis: Like humans, LLMs do not produce their best output first try, and the same LLM can supply useful feedback and use it to improve (stated in the abstract and introduction).
contributions: SELF-REFINE: an iterative FEEDBACK-REFINE loop using one LLM as generator, feedback provider and refiner, with few-shot prompts and no training
Evaluation on 7 tasks with GPT-3.5, ChatGPT and GPT-4 (and Codex for code), including two new tasks, Acronym Generation and Constrained Generation (CommonGen-Hard)
Ablations on feedback quality, number of iterations, multiple-sample baseline and a weaker model (Vicuna-13B)

method.summary: Given input x, the model produces y0 from a few-shot generation prompt, then alternates a few-shot FEEDBACK prompt (fb_t from x and y_t) and a few-shot REFINE prompt (y_t+1 from x, all earlier outputs and feedback) until a stop condition or a maximum number of iterations. Compared with the same base LLM generating once.
method.task: test-time iterative refinement across dialogue, code optimisation, code readability, math reasoning, sentiment reversal, acronym generation, constrained generation

inference.decoding: 'greedy decoding with a temperature of 0.7 for all setups' (as printed; internally contradictory). Appendix L: critique at T=0.0 and T=0.7, code editor always T=0.0.
inference.samples: One SELF-REFINE run per item (not stated). 1-vs-k check: ChatGPT generates k=4 samples without feedback and SELF-REFINE is compared with all k.
inference.prompting: Few-shot prompts for generation, feedback and refine, even for ChatGPT and GPT-4. Examples: Acronym 15 (title, acronym) pairs, 3 for feedback and refine; Dialogue 6 examples for feedback in 4.1 (Appendix M.1) but 3 for init/feedback/iterate in M.2; Math 2 examples from GSM8K train on which Codex fails; Constrained Gen 10 init examples; Code Opt uses PIE slow/fast pairs and explanations.

parameters.max_iterations: 4 (Section 3.1); Dialogue k=3 (App. M.2); Sentiment k=4 (App. P); Code Readability N=5 (App. L)
parameters.stop_condition: fixed iteration count or a stop indicator extracted from the feedback (e.g. scalar score), set per task
parameters.history: all previous outputs and feedback are appended to the REFINE prompt (Eq. 4)
parameters.output_selection: Dialogue and Acronym: output with highest total feedback score across iterations (excluding the initial response for Dialogue); otherwise the last refinement y_t

other.oracle_feedback_math: App. H.1: only refine when the current answer is incorrect, following Welleck et al. 2022

metrics.name: Human-pref
metrics.definition: blind A/B between baseline and SELF-REFINE outputs; tie options; done by the authors

metrics.name: GPT-4-pref
metrics.definition: GPT-4 as proxy judge for Sentiment Reversal, Acronym, Dialogue; for Code Readability GPT-4 computes fraction of variables appropriately named

baselines: Same base LLM with one-step generation
PaL, CoT, PIE, Scalene, CodeGen (Appendix F)
eval.protocol: GPT-4-pref correlation with human-pref reported as 82% (Sentiment), 68% (Acronym), 71% (Dialogue). Wilson intervals in Table 13. Human A/B on 150 examples per dataset (Table 6). No seeds reported.

limits: Base models need sufficient few-shot or instruction-following ability; Vicuna-13B failed (Limitations, Section 4).
All main models are closed (GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, GPT-4, Codex), details undisclosed and paid; English only; no safeguard against toxic steering (Section 6).
Math Reasoning gains are near zero without an external correctness signal because the model cannot detect its own errors.
Human A/B evaluation was done by the authors, and GPT-4-pref correlation with humans is only 68-82%.
Per-iteration averages in Fig 4 pool three models; no seeds or repeated runs reported; many gains are not significant for GPT-3.5 and ChatGPT.
Baseline is the same LLM generating once, not compute-matched against multiple samples, except the k=4 human 1-vs-k test.
Paper is internally inconsistent in places: temperature 'greedy ... 0.7', Table 1 vs Tables 7/8 numbers, 95% vs 99% intervals, 372 vs 342 dialogue instances, an unfinished 'TODO' line in Appendix S.
